The company own site confirms Chicago as one of its three data center markets, alongside Austin and Houston, Texas, though Wood Dale specifically was not individually named. Element Critical describes itself as a data center infrastructure provider specializing in high density power and advanced cooling for demanding workloads including AI and GPU infrastructure, offering colocation from individual cabinets to custom suites supporting deployments up to 50 megawatts. No founding date, headquarters address, ownership structure, or building specific address and MW figures for this particular registry row were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Element Critical's Wood Dale facility publishes 7 MW of IT capacity across 151,000 square feet, enough to support 175 to 700 racks depending on workload density, though the operator does not disclose how power is actually distributed.

The three published certifications—PCI DSS, HIPAA, and ISO 27001—qualify the site for regulated workloads in finance and healthcare. None address the infrastructure requirements for AI training, such as high-density power delivery or low-latency interconnect between GPUs. The operator has published no technical specifications on those points, making the facility's suitability for large-scale compute difficult to assess from available data.

Among the 44 Illinois data centers this site has mapped, only 6 publish a megawatt figure. CH2's 7 MW ranks fifth within that disclosed subset and represents roughly 3 percent of Illinois's published total capacity. This modest ranking reflects either a smaller footprint than the state's largest campuses or a partial disclosure of the site's actual capability. The operator has not clarified which.
